title.en: Area of a circle and an ellipse

heading.en: Why is the area of a circle πr²?

hook.en: Since school you have used πr² for the area of a *circle*. Today integration proves it, and gives us the area of an ellipse, the shape of planetary orbits, as a bonus.
hook.kn: ಶಾಲೆಯಿಂದಲೂ ವೃತ್ತದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣಕ್ಕೆ πr² ಬಳಸಿದ್ದೀರಿ. ಇಂದು ಅನುಕಲನ ಅದನ್ನು ಸಾಬೀತುಪಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಗ್ರಹಗಳ ಕಕ್ಷೆಯ ಆಕಾರವಾದ ದೀರ್ಘವೃತ್ತದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣವನ್ನೂ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Derive the area of a circle using integration
Derive the area of an ellipse as πab

say.en: Since school you have used pi r squared for the area of a circle. Today integration proves it, and gives us the area of an ellipse, the shape of planetary orbits, as a bonus. In this lesson: Derive the area of a circle using integration.
Derive the area of an ellipse as pi ab.
Use symmetry of the four quadrants.

title.en: Area of the circle x² + y² = a²

body.en: The *circle* is symmetric in all four quadrants. In the first quadrant $y = \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}$. Using $\int\sqrt{a^2-x^2}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2-x^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{a}$, the quarter area is $\frac{\pi a^2}{4}$, so the whole area is $\pi a^2$.
body.kn: ವೃತ್ತ ನಾಲ್ಕೂ ಚತುರ್ಥಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮಮಿತ. ಮೊದಲ ಚತುರ್ಥಕದಲ್ಲಿ y = √(a² − x²). ಕಾಲು ಭಾಗದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πa²/4, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಪೂರ್ಣ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πa².

points.en: The standard integral of √(a² − x²) is the key

narration.en: The circle is symmetric in all four quadrants. In the first quadrant y is the square root of a squared minus x squared. Integrating from 0 to a gives pi a squared by 4, so the full area is pi a squared.
narration.kn: ವೃತ್ತ ನಾಲ್ಕೂ ಚತುರ್ಥಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮಮಿತ. ಮೊದಲ ಚತುರ್ಥಕದಲ್ಲಿ y = √(a² − x²). ಕಾಲು ಭಾಗದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πa²/4, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಪೂರ್ಣ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πa².

say.en: The circle is symmetric in all four quadrants. In the first quadrant y is the square root of a squared minus x squared. Integrating from 0 to a gives pi a squared by 4, so the full area is pi a squared. Area equals 4 times (first-quadrant area).
say.kn: ವೃತ್ತ ನಾಲ್ಕೂ ಚತುರ್ಥಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮಮಿತ. ಮೊದಲ ಚತುರ್ಥಕದಲ್ಲಿ y equals the square root of (a squared - x squared). ಕಾಲು ಭಾಗದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ pi a squared/4, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಪೂರ್ಣ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ pi a squared.

title.en: Circle and ellipse from one integral

narration.en: The teacher finds the area of a circle by four quarter regions, then stretches it into an ellipse.

say.en: Here is the circle x squared plus y squared equals a squared. By symmetry, its area is four times the quarter in the first quadrant.
In the first quadrant, y = root of a squared minus x squared. Take vertical strips from 0 to a.
Use the standard integral. At x = a the inverse sine gives pi by 2, and everything else is zero.
For an ellipse, y is b over a times the same root. So the area is b over a times the circle area: pi a b.
For a = 4 and b = 3, the area is 12 pi square units.
The teacher finds the area of a circle by four quarter regions, then stretches it into an ellipse.

narration.en: Sweep a vertical strip across the first quadrant of x²/a² + y²/b² = 1. The quarter area is πab/4, so the whole ellipse has area πab. A circle is the case a = b.
narration.kn: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 ರ ಮೊದಲ ಚತುರ್ಥದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಂಬ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ. ಕಾಲು ಭಾಗದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πab/4, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇಡೀ ದೀರ್ಘವೃತ್ತದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πab. a = b ಆದಾಗ ವೃತ್ತ.

title.en: Area of the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1

body.en: In the first quadrant $y = \frac{b}{a}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}$. So the area is $4\cdot\frac{b}{a}\cdot\frac{\pi a^2}{4} = \pi ab$. When $a = b$ the *ellipse* becomes a circle and the formula becomes $\pi a^2$.
body.kn: ಮೊದಲ ಚತುರ್ಥಕದಲ್ಲಿ y = (b/a)√(a² − x²). ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ದೀರ್ಘವೃತ್ತದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πab. a = b ಆದಾಗ ಅದು ವೃತ್ತ, ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ πa².

problem.en: Find the area enclosed by the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1.

steps.en: Here a = 4 and b = 3; in the first quadrant y = (3/4)√(16 − x²).
= 3 · (8 · π/2) = 12π sq. units, which matches πab = π·4·3.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the area enclosed by the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the area enclosed by the ellipse x squared/16 plus y squared/9 equals 1.
Here a equals 4 and b equals 3; in the first quadrant y equals (3 over 4) the square root of (16 - x squared).

Area equals 4 (3 over 4) the integral of 0 to the power 4 the square root of (16 - x squared) dx equals 3 [(x over 2) the square root of (16 - x squared) plus 8 sin to the power minus 1(x over 4)] 0 to the power 4.
= 3 (8 pi /2) equals 12 pi sq. units, which matches pi ab equals pi 4 3.
So the answer is 12 pi sq. units.

body.en: Remember just one formula, πab, for the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1. For a circle put b = a. Always bring the equation to the form with 1 on the right before reading a and b.
